issue.title: Quarkus requires `{` and `}` to be URL encoded in the query param
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

I have hit a strange issue that Quarkus requires `{` and `}` to be URL-encoded in the query param value.. Seems that different clients choose different behavior wrt encoding those chars, and it's kind of a gray area.. There are bunch of RFCs that define different approaches, and the [WHATWG (URL) standards](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/) that specifies that for query params these chars does not have to be encoded.

Some clients, for example Postman (from version `8.0` and up), will not URL encode the `{` and `}` when those are in the query param value. In the same way, some HTTP server implementations do not require those to be encoded. With Quarkus, any HTTP request that has `{` or `}` non encoded in the query value will fail with `400`. 

Now I am not interested here in going into deeper discussion on what's the right approach. But the previous HTTP server implementation we used allowed those chars to be not-encoded and our new services are now failing those requests. This means we are breaking the backward-compatibility in a way.

I would like to know if there is any way to change this behavior? Any property, specification, anything that we could quickly use to fix the issue. Any solution is fine, maybe an interceptor that can perform additional encoding or something like this :pray:

issue.title: disabe vert.x uri validation in the v2 docker images
issue.body:
**What this PR does**:
The `-Dvertx.disableURIValidation=true` works and disables the URI validation, but can not be defined in the `application.yaml` config.. I had no other idea, then actually adding this to the docker image.. Or should we leave this as optional in the deployment?

Another thing I noticed in the docker images is `JAVA_OPTS` and `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND`. Would defining a `JAVA_OPTS` in the container during deployment actually overwrite what I added? We need to use the `JAVA_OPTS_APPEND` then..

It would be nice to have a test for this, will try to add one maybe.
